text: On 26 October 2024, Telangana State Police (TGSP) personnel from the 12th Battalion along with a former BRS MLA staged a protest in Aneparti village (Nalgonda, Telangana) demanding the INC-led state government to fulfil their demands which included reducing their long working hours and granting leaves. The protesters shouted slogans to mark their protest and the police arrested the BRS leader.

On 26 October 2024, villagers continued to stage a hunger strike protest in Gummalladoddi village (East Godavari, Andhra Pradesh) against the functioning of the Assago Ethanol factory in the village. The protesters demanded the authorities to relocate the factory citing health and pollution concerns. The police detained protesters who were hiding in a temple fearing police action along with 15 another persons.

On 26 October 2024, hundreds of INC members including a former minister took out a protest march to the District Collectorate in Pathanamthitta town (Kerala) demanding a judicial investigation into the suicide of an Additional District Magistrate (ADM) after a former district panchayat president levelled corruption charges against him at a public event. The protesters accused the LDF-led state government of trying to save the culprits and climbed up the barricades set by the police. The protesters then had an altercation with the police, though the details of the altercation have not been specified.

On 26 October 2024, members of the CPI(M) staged a protest at the Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Corporation Limited (CPDCL) office at the Alankar Centre in Vijayawada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) demanding the TDP-led state government to revoke the permission given to the electricity board by the Andhra Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (APERC) to recover Fuel and Power Purchase Cost Adjustment (FPPCA) charges from the consumers for the electricity they consumed in the 2022-23 financial year.

On 26 October 2024, residents including members of the Adi Dravidar (Dalit) community staged a protest in Semmangudy village (Nagapattinam, Tamil Nadu) demanding the authorities to take measures to repair the bad condition of the roads in the village. The protesters planted saplings on the road to mark their protest.

Around 26 October 2024 (as reported), members of several youth organisations including the DYFI staged a protest at the Secunderabad Railway Station in Secunderabad city (Medchal-Malkajgiri, Telangana) against the Railway Board's decision to fill the vacant posts in the railways with retired employees. The protesters demanded the authorities to provide opportunities to unemployed youngsters.
On 26 October 2024, DYFI members held a protest march at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) over the disappearance of a new-born's body from a hospital.

On 26 October 2024, locals and members of farmers' organisations staged a protest near the Kelavarapalli reservoir on the Karnataka-Tamil Nadu border in Kelavarapalli village (Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu) against the thick layer of froth that had formed in the reservoir due to the sewage and untreated effluents from industries that were being released into the water body and had spilled out onto the roads.

On 26 October 2024, hundreds of students staged a protest and burned an effigy near the Clock Tower in Dehradun city (Uttarakhand) condemning the state government's decision to cancel student union elections.

On 26 October 2024, farmers under the banner of KMM staged an indefinite protest 'Day 1' along the Sangrur-Bathinda highway in Sangrur city (Punjab) against the state government whom the protesters accused of failing to ensure the smooth procurement of paddy crops.

On 26 October 2024, farmers under the banner of KMM staged an indefinite protest 'Day 1' along the Moga-Ferozepur highway in Moga city (Punjab) against the state government whom the protesters accused of failing to ensure the smooth procurement of paddy crops.

On 26 October 2024, farmers under the banner of KMM staged an indefinite protest 'Day 1' along the Gurdaspur-Tanda highway in Sathiali village (Gurdaspur, Punjab) against the state government whom the protesters accused of failing to ensure the smooth procurement of paddy crops.

On 26 October 2024, farmers under the banner of KMM staged an indefinite protest 'Day 1' at the railway station in Batala city (Gurdaspur, Punjab) against the state government whom the protesters accused of failing to ensure the smooth procurement of paddy crops.

On 26 October 2024, family members of the deceased staged a dharna (sit-in protest) at the Mini Secretariat in Hisar city (Haryana) against the suicide of a man (retired soldier) who the protesters claimed was harassed by the police. A case has been registered against 10 accused, including a former Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP).
On 26 October 2024, many BJP members and local people staged a protest at the Haathi Wala Pul area in Aligarh city (Uttar Pradesh) against the dumping of Indian flags in the garbage.

On 26 October 2024, farmers and members of SKM (Non-political) and KMM staged an indefinite protest along the Ludhiana-Ferozepur highway in Dagru village (Moga, Punjab) against the state government whom the protesters accused of failing to ensure the smooth procurement of paddy crops.

On 26 October 2024, farmers and members of SKM (Non-political) and KMM staged an indefinite protest along the Bathinda-Zirakpur national highway in Badrukhan village (Sangrur, Punjab) against the state government whom the protesters accused of failing to ensure the smooth procurement of paddy crops.

On 26 October 2024, farmers and members of BKU (Ekta Sidhupur) staged a protest along the Bathinda-Mansa Road in Jassi Pauwali village (Bathinda, Punjab) against the state government whom the protesters accused of failing to ensure the smooth procurement of paddy crops.

On 26 October 2024, junior doctors and entertainment professionals held a candle and torch protest march at Kolkata city (WB) against non-fulfilment of demands by the state government including removal of the health secretary and action against 'threat culture', over the Kolkata doctor rape-murder case and demanded a faster investigation by the central bureau of investigation.

On 26 October 2024, INC supporters held a sit-in protest in Sangamner town (Ahmednagar district, Maharashtra) demanding immediate action against the supporter of former BJP Ahmednagar MP who used derogatory words against the daughter of incumbent Congress MLA and former pradesh congress party president, ahead of the state assembly elections.

On 26 October 2024, members of the INC including a former Union minister staged a protest in front of Tirupati Municipal Corporation office in Tirupati city (Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh) questioning why the TDP-led state government was acquiring 50,000 acres of land to build the state capital in Amaravati. The protesters also condemned the delay in the completion of the capital city.

On 26 October 2024, members of the Kerala Water Authority Staff Association affiliated to the INTUC staged a protest in Aluva town (Ernakulam, Kerala) against the LDF-led state government's proposal to privatise the water supply system in Kochi city.

On 26 October 2024, farmers staged protests at districts under the Malwa region in the Punjab state (coded as Chandigarh city) against the state government whom the protesters accused of failing to ensure the smooth procurement of paddy crops.

On 26 October 2024, around 300 farmer union members were joined by the KMSC coordinator and BKU (Doaba) president on 'Day 6' of their dharna (sit-in protest) at Sugar Mill Chowk (intersection) in Phagwara city (Kapurthala, Punjab) against the state government whom the protesters accused of failing to ensure the smooth procurement of paddy crops.

On 26 October 2024, local people (likely from the Dalit community since the issue involved the removal of a statue of a Dalit champion) staged a protest in Bakarpur village (Yamunanagar, Haryana) against the local administration for removing the statue of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar (a Dalit champion). The protesters scuffled with the police and a dozen protesters were detained.

On 26 October 2024, several people including tiatrists (performer in the Konkani-language musical theatre) under the aegis of the Global Konkani Forum (GKF), the Mandd Sobhan-Mangaluru, and the Konknni Lekhak Sangh Association, took out a silent protest march in Margao city (South Goa, Goa) against the discrimination of the Roman and other scripts and in support of the writing of the Konkani language in the Roman script. The protesters also demanded the dissolution of the Advisory Committee of the Sahitya Akademi.

On 26 October 2024, members of the PDP staged a protest outside the Kerala NGO Union Hall in Kozhikode city (Kerala) against a book that was written by a former MLA and CPI(M) state committee member which contained derogatory references to the PDP founder. The protesters raised slogans and burned the cover pages of the book to mark their protest while the Kerala Chief Minister was releasing the book inside the hall.

On 26 October 2024, several Telangana State Police (TGSP) constables from the Mamnoor Fourth Battalion staged a protest in front of the Battalion Commandant's office in Mamnoor village (Warangal Urban, Telangana) demanding the INC-led state government to fulfil their demands which included reducing their long working hours and granting leaves.

On 26 October 2024, a large number of women along with the children of Telangana State Police (TGSP) personnel took out a protest march in Kothagudem town (Bhadradri Kothagudem, Telangana) demanding the INC-led state government to fulfil their demands which included reducing their long working hours and granting leaves. The protesters shouted slogans to mark their protest.

On 26 October 2024, members of an organization (night is ours) held a protest march at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) over the Kolkata doctor rape-murder case and to demand protection for women at night and swift investigation by the central bureau of investigation.

On 26 October 2024, villagers of Honavad staged a protest in front of the Deputy Commissioner's office in Bijapur city (Vijayapura, Karnataka) against the notices that farmers received from the Waqf (dedication of property for any purpose recognised by Muslim law as religious or charitable) Board notifying them that their land was being taken over by the board. The protesters demanded the authorities to withdraw the notices.

On 26 October 2024, family members of Telangana State Police (TGSP) personnel staged protests across Telangana state (coded to Hyderabad) demanding the INC-led state government to ensure better working conditions and facilities for the officers.

Around 26 October 2024 (as reported), citizens staged a protest at the Subhash Chowrasta in Pebbair town (Wanaparthy, Telangana) against a person who was planning to buy the government-owned municipal centre that housed the Pebbair market and had attempted to block access to the market.

On 26 October 2024, scores residents staged a protest in Ranastalam town (Srikakulam, Andhra Pradesh) against the proposed construction of a six-lane highway and elevated bridge in the town as existing shops and buildings would have to be demolished in the process.

On 26 October 2024, AAP Youth Shakti staged a protest in Guwahati city (Kamrup Metropolitan, Assam) condemning BJP government and demanded the withdrawal of smart meters and to control the increase in prices for essential commodities, medical, and electricity services.

On 26 October 2024, organisations representing locals of Biswanath Chariali including Sangrami Yuba Chatra Parishad (SYCPA), All Guwahati Students' Union (AGSU), AASU, AJYCP, All Assam Adivasi Students Association (AAASA), Bir Lachit Sena staged a road block protest and submitted a memorandum to the District Commissioner in Biswanath town (Biswanath, Assam) condemning National Highway Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited (NHIDCL) and Assam government for their inability to finish the four lane project and bypass along National Highway 15, pending for 8 years.

On 26 October 2024, hundreds of women IDPs staged a sit in protest at their temporary houses near Sajiwa jail on the outskirts of Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) condemning their prolonged displacement and demanded Manipur government for a resolution while announcing their decision to boycott an upcoming important local Meitei festival.
On 26 October 2024, street vendors started a dharna (sit-in protest) in Badadanda (Grand Road) at Puri city (Odisha) demanding a designated area to carry out their business.

On 27 October 2024, members of the BRS staged a protest outside a private villa community in the Raidurgam locality in Hyderabad city (Telangana) after the police and the Excise department attempted to enter the villas of BRS leaders and their relatives without search warrants. Police arrested 20 protesters.

On 27 October 2024, farmers along with members of the INC including an MP and MLAs took a protest march in Thungathurthi village (Suryapet, Telangana) in support of the INC-led state government's Musi river development project. The protesters also accused the BRS of running a propaganda against the INC.

On 27 October 2024, Himalayan Nature and Adventure Foundation and the Indian Medical Association held a protest march at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) against the use of crackers during festivals.

On 27 October 2024, citizens along with an Independent MLA and a former INC minister under the aegis of the Sancoale Against Mega Project (SAMP) staged a protest in Sancoale town (South Goa, Goa) against the proposed multi-dwelling house project by the Bhutani Infra Development group. The protesters also expressed their solidarity with a former Sarpanch who was on an indefinite hunger strike demanding the revocation of the licence issued for the Bhutani project.

On 27 October 2024, local people and family members of the deceased staged a protest in Gauspur village (Shravasti, Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a boy who was crushed to death by a speeding bus. The protesters caught the bus driver and handed him over to the police.

On 27 October 2024, a large number of local people, including family members of the deceased and an SP leader, staged a sit-in protest outside the Mantri Awas Campus in Lucknow city (Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a man who the protesters claimed was tortured and killed by the police while under detention. The police detained the SP leader.

On 27 October 2024, several local people, including Bajrang Dal members, assaulted two young people from the Muslim community near the Sohna Flyover in the Faridabad district (Haryana) over suspicions of carrying cow meat.

On 27 October 2024, 35 local people staged a protest along the Maharajganj-Inhauna Road near Khekharuwa village (Amethi, Uttar Pradesh) against the Public Works Department (PWD) whom the protesters accused of poor quality of construction work on the Maharajganj-Inhauna road.
On 27 October 2024, two groups of people clashed, using sticks and stones, in Bahadurpur village (Amroha, Uttar Pradesh) over a land dispute. Six people were injured, including a policeman.

On 27 October 2024, local people and commuters staged a protest, carrying placards and raising slogans, near the Nandpur railway station in Ghanban village (Kangra, Himachal Pradesh) against the failure to restore railway operations from Nurpur road to Kangra railway stations.

On 27 October 2024, family members of the deceased staged a demonstration and vandalized property at the Shekhar Saraf Hospital in Aligarh city (Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a man who the demonstrators claimed died due to the hospital's negligence - administration of the wrong injection. The hospital staff retaliated and assaulted the demonstrators. Members also staged a demonstration and clashed with the police near the Agra Road Hospital on the same day.

On 27 October 2024, teachers from Adarsh School joined by BKU (Totewal) members staged a protest outside the house of an AAP MP in Barnala city (Punjab) against the failure of the state government to address their long-standing demands including improved salaries. The protesters removed a police barricade and scuffled (likely non-violent based on similar coded events) with the police - during which a protester was injured. The protesters also accused the police of beating them.

On 27 October 2024, family members of a deceased child and members of Anjuman Khidmat Khalk organisation (a Muslim group) held a protest at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) over claimed medical negligence leading to the child's death.

On 27 October 2024, Telangana State Police (TGSP) personnel from the 12th Battalion staged a protest in Nalgonda city (Telangana) demanding the authorities to reinstate the 39 TGSP personnel who were suspended for staging a protest demanding the INC-led state government to ensure better working conditions and facilities (coded separately).

On 27 October 2024, members of the Telangana Special Police (TGSP) from the 17th battalion staged a protest in Sircilla town (Rajanna Sircilla, Telangana) demanding the authorities to reinstate the six TGSP personnel who were dismissed for protesting against their work conditions.
On 27 October 2024, Bharat-Tibet Sahyog Manch (a Tibetan ethnic group) held a protest march at Jammu city (J&K) against China and demanded boycott of Chinese products.

On 27 October 2024, residents staged a silent protest during a general body meeting of the Anjuna comunidade in Anjuna village (North Goa, Goa) against the proposal to conduct large-scale electronic dance and music events in the village.

On 27 October 2024, locals staged a protest in Cavelossim village (South Goa, Goa) against the destruction of a sand dune and plants in a property near a bridge in the village. The protesters also opposed the proposed construction of a road nearby.

On 27 October 2024, residents of Pragathi Nagar near Nizampet staged a protest in the locality in Hyderabad city (Telangana) demanding the Pollution Control Board (PCB) authorities to take action against a local pharmaceutical factory for releasing a 'toxic gas' which emanated a foul smell and caused health issues among the residents.

On 27 October 2024, locals, after a fatal accident, blocked the Khadial-Bhawanipatna road and held a protest at Chandotara Square under Sindhekela Police Station (Bolangir district, Odisha) demanding adequate compensation for the family members of a deceased.
On 27 October 2024, locals of Bogibeel area physically assaulted 5 persons, detained them and turned them over to the police in Dibrugarh town (Dibrugarh, Assam) over suspicions of cattle theft.

On 27 October 2024, a large number of locals staged a road block protest, a sit in protest and blocked NH-102 at Khangabok market, Wangbal Khongnang Makhong and Arong Thong in Khangabok village (Thoubal, Manipur) condemning the threat to family members and grenade scare at the residence of Sur Hospital's proprietor (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 27 October 2024, members of the Purani Pension Bahali Sangharsh Committee (old pension restoration struggle committee) staged a protest in Gidderbaha town (Sri Muktsar Sahib, Punjab) over various demands.

On 27 October 2024, 200 workers staged a protest outside the residences of two JCT Mill directors in Phagwara city (Kapurthala, Punjab) against the non-payment of bonuses, allowances, and salaries. One of the directors fired a shot at the protesters - the police suspect that it could have been in self-defense. There were no injuries. The police have registered a case against the director.

On 28 October 2024, members of the Telangana Special Police (TGSP) staged a protest at the Dharna Chowk in Hyderabad city (Telangana) demanding the INC-led state government to fulfil their demands which included reducing their long working hours and granting leaves. Police arrested 21 protesters.

On 28 October 2024, hundreds of members of the BJP staged a protest at the office of the District Police Chief (Kannur City) in Kannur city (Kerala) demanding action against a former district panchayat president after an Additional District Magistrate (ADM) died by suicide after the district panchayat president levelled corruption charges against him at a public event. Police used water cannons to disperse the protesters which led to 'skirmishes' between the two groups. The protesters sustained injuries and were detained by the police.

On 28 October 2024, a group of women surrounded SDM's vehicle, during a visit by the officials to dissuade the villagers from staging a march to the district headquarters, and held a protest in Patharra village (Bemetara district, Chhattisgarh) against filing of charges on two of their comrades by the police for their role in the ongoing agitation against the establishment of an ethanol plant. Female police officers used some force to disperse the women protestors. A few women sustained minor injuries. Officials have clarified that police did not use lathicharge against them.

On 28 October 2024, a group of people gathered and burned the effigy of Bihar police outside the residence of the chief minister in Patna city (Bihar) during a protest against claimed Police inaction in a hit-and-run case in Danapur. Police detained the leader of the protest.

On 28 October 2024, hundreds of students under the aegis of the AIDSO staged a protest in front of Crawford Hall at the University of Mysore in Mysuru city (Karnataka) demanding the authorities to postpone the examinations and withdraw the increase in the examination and marks card fees.

On 28 October 2024, members of the BJP staged a protest in front of the office of Sirpur (T) forest range officer in Sirpur town (Kumuram Bheem Asifabad, Telangana) accusing two forest range officers of manhandling persons who were arrested in a poaching case. The protesters demanded action against the forest officials.

On 28 October 2024, members of the CPI Telangana Rythu Sangham (farmers group) staged a protest at the Collectorate in Khammam city (Telangana) demanding the INC-led state government to issue crop loan waivers to all eligible farmers.

On 28 October 2024, villagers and members of the DSS took out a protest march to the Deputy Commissioner's office in Shimoga city (Shivamogga, Karnataka) demanding the district administration authorities to ensure that the Dalit families of Kachagondanahalli in Bhadravati taluk got back the land that was granted to them by the government.

On 28 October 2024, farmers and members of several groups staged protests in Vijayapura district (coded to Bijapur city, Karnataka) against the notices that farmers received in Vijayapura district from the Waqf (dedication of property for any purpose recognised by Muslim law as religious or charitable) Board notifying them that their land was being taken over by the board. The protesters demanded the authorities to withdraw the notices.

On 28 October 2024, hundreds of paramedical workers under the aegis of the Odisha government outsourcing paramedical employees association held a protest at Lower PMG square in Bhubaneswar city (Khordha, Odisha), over various demands including a permanent job, appointment through NHM instead of an outsourcing agency and re-appointment of those discontinued from their jobs.

On 28 October 2024, INC councillors staged a protest during the monthly council meeting of Hubballi-Dharwad Municipal Corporation in Dharwad city (Karnataka) against the allegations made by the BJP councillors that the INC-led state government did not have funds for development projects.

On 28 October 2024, INC and UDF councillors and members of the INC and the KSU staged separate protests in Kannur city (Kerala) demanding the removal of the district panchayat president after an Additional District Magistrate (ADM) died by suicide after the district panchayat president levelled corruption charges against him at a public event.

On 28 October 2024, members of the IUML including a former MP staged a protest at the Menka Junction in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) accusing the LDF-led state government of using 'communal' tactics for vote bank politics.

On 28 October 2024, candidates aspiring to be Hindi and Sanskrit teachers staged mock classes under trees and held a protest at Lower PMG square in Bhubaneswar city (Khordha, Odisha), against the appointment of non-Hindi & Sanskrit teachers in the posts meant for Hindi and Sanskrit teachers.

On 28 October 2024, workers of the Tamil Nadu Tea Plantation Corporation (TANTEA) along with members of the Socialist Thozhilalar Munnetra Sangam (Socialist Labor Advancement Association) staged a protest near the TANTEA office headquarters in Coonoor town (The Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu) demanding the authorities to increase their Diwali (Hindu festival) bonus.

On 28 October 2024, shopkeepers and traders held a protest and a shutter down strike at Ganderbal city (J&K) over absence of essential services, including drainage, regular power supply, and street lights.

On 28 October 2024, a large number of workers held a protest at the accident site in Patna city (Bihar) after two workers from Odisha were killed and six others injured in an accident at an under-construction tunnel of the Patna metro rail.

On 28 October 2024, Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) agents under the aegis of the All India Life Insurance Agents Federation staged a protest in front of the Rajamahendravaram rural branch and main branch offices in Rajahmundry city (East Godavari, Andhra Pradesh) demanding the company to stop the proposal to reduce the agents' commissions and adjust the commissions over a six-year period. The protesters also demanded the revocation of a recent proposal to reduce the age limit for policyholders.
On 28 October 2024, sanitation workers staged a sit-in protest in Shenkottai town (Tenkasi, Tamil Nadu) demanding the municipality authorities to give them a Diwali (Hindu festival) bonus.

On 28 October 2024, members of the Punjab and Chandigarh College Teachers' Union staged a candlelight protest march to Bharat Nagar Chowk (intersection) from Guru Nanak Dev Bhawan (a building) in Ludhiana city (Punjab) over various issues including the reduction of the age limit for principals, and non-implementation of the 7th pay commission.

On 28 October 2024, members of the AgriGold Customers and Agents Welfare Association, along with members of the CPI, the CPI(M) including a former minister and an MLC and members of several organisations staged a day-long protest at the Dharna Chowk in Vijayawada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) demanding the TDP-led state government to solve the issues of the victims by taking the properties of the AgriGold Group and repaying the money of the depositors.

On 28 October 2024, students from Soban Singh Jeena (SSJ) University (likely including NSUI members since an NSUI leader had threatened to immolate himself earlier) staged a protest at Chauganpata area in Almora town (Uttarakhand) condemning the state government's decision to cancel student union elections. A protester who had set himself on fire was rushed to the hospital and the rest of the protesters continued their protest and burned effigies.

On 28 October 2024, students from various districts gathered and staged a protest march - styled as a funeral procession - from INC Bhawan (office) to the Secretariat in Dehradun city (Uttarakhand) condemning the state government's decision to cancel student union elections.

On 15 January 2025, SFI members held a protest by burning an effigy at Bardhaman city (Purba Bardhaman district, WB) against the TMC-led state government over claimed procurement of sub-standard medical substance leading to a patient's death.
On 15 January 2025, residents held a protest at Ladoora town (Baramulla district, J&K) over illegal extraction of sand claiming it had damaged the river Jhelum embankments and the horticulture lands.

On 15 January 2025, six people were suspected of assaulting two young men and a Dalit woman - who was also stripped - with sharp-edged weapons at a village under the Kheri police station area (Uttar Pradesh) over a dispute between the assailants and one of the young men. The woman suffered deep cut wounds and one man lost a finger.

On 15 January 2025, some people, led by an electricity contractor, assaulted two Hindu saints (priests) at an electricity repair warehouse, close to the Old GT River Front crossing, in Allahabad city (Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh) when the two priests arrived at the warehouse to register a complaint regarding lack of power supply at the ashram (Hindu religious dwelling). The assailants were also accused of stealing a gold chain. The rioters later also assaulted another group of Hindu saints who had arrived to confront them about the earlier assault.

Around 15 January 2025 (month of), nearly 200 landowners 'stormed' the office of Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) office in Kengeri and staged a protest in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) against the disconnection of electrical power supply from their homes.
Around 15 January 2025 (month of), farmers staged protests in Dilawarpur village (Nirmal, Telangana) against the construction of an ethanol factory.

On 16 January 2025, HNYF staged a protest in Shillong city (East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya) against the establishment of the Invest Meghalaya Authority (IMA) which would lease land to private companies for setting up industries in the state. Protesters also highlighted the Meghalaya Transfer of Land (Regulation) Act, 1971 which prohibits the sale of land to non-tribal entities.

On 16 January 2025, Kairembikhok residents (likely laborers based on reason for protest) and Meira Paibi activists staged a sit in protest with placards at Kairembikhok Lamkhai's waiting shed in Kairembikhok village (Thoubal, Manipur) condemning the excessive monetary demands made by various organizations (likely armed based on similar events) on daily wage earners in the area, citing financial difficulties amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 16 January 2025, hundreds of tea tribe community members staged a gherao (surround) protest and blocked Lahowal police station in Lahowal village (Dibrugarh, Assam) demanding justice for a girl who was murdered and suspectedly raped.

On 16 January 2025, hundreds of Chaulkhowa residents staged a protest march with placards and banners in Chaulkhowa village (Dibrugarh, Assam) against the BJP-led tate government's inability to implement an important river bank erosion control project at Bogibeel (river) announced by the Water Resources Minister in August 2024.

On 16 January 2025, several BRS leaders and members staged a protest at the Enforcement Directorate (ED) office in Basheerbagh in Hyderabad city (Telangana) after a BRS MLA was asked to appear before the ED for questioning in connection with a Formula-E car race case. The protesters argued with the police, following which several protesters were detained.
On 16 January 2025, members of the KRRS staged a protest in Belagavi city (Karnataka) opposing the supply of water from the Hidkal damn to the industrial areas of Hubballi and Dharwad.

On 16 January 2025, members of the Akhila Bharat Veerashaiva Mahasabha (Lingayat group) staged a protest in Yadgir city (Karnataka) condemning the incident in which a minor girl was found dead in Jewargi town and the desecration Basaveshwara statue in Dagadi village (coded separately).

On 16 January 2025, members of Karnataka Rajya Hiriya Nagarikara Kshemabhivrudhi Sangha (Karnataka State Senior Citizens Welfare Development Association) staged a massive protest rally from Nehru Maidan to Chennamma Circle in Hubballi city (Dharwad, Karnataka) demanding rights and recognition including a separate ministry for senior citizens, rupees 10,000 for Below Poverty Line (BPL) card holders, and the announcement of senior citizens as a national asset. The protesters raised slogans against both the BJP-led Union government and the INC-led state government.

On 16 January 2025, BEd students held a dharna (sit-in protest) on the RNT Marg campus of Devi Ahilya Vishwavidyalaya (DAVV) in Indore city (Madhya Pradesh) demanding a special fourth attempt for the examination of the two-year course.

On 16 January 2025, hundreds of farmers and BKMU members, joined by the INLD state president, staged a protest along Kaithal Road and freed the toll plaza next to Thana village (Kurukshetra, Haryana) in support of the 'Delhi Chalo' (let's go to Delhi) protests led by SKM (Non-political) and KMM, and the fast-unto-death by a farmer leader - who were demanding the provision of a legal guarantee for the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for crops, debt waivers for farmers, compensation for family members of farmers who died during previous protests, pension for laborers and farmers, and implementation of the Land Acquisition Act (2013) and Swaminathan Commission's recommendations.

On 16 January 2025, local people, including the Sarpanch (village administration chief) representative, staged a protest in Pichopa Kalan village (Charkhi Dadri, Haryana) against a mining company whom the protesters accused of carrying out mining in the area beyond the permissible limit - a portion of rock also fell on the mining site, injuring one worker, due to suspected illegal mining.

On 16 January 2025, students staged a protest at Bhagat Phool Singh Women's Medical College in Khanpur Kalan village (Sonipat, Haryana) against the expulsion of six students over accusations of ragging. The protesters claimed that the accusations were false.

On 16 January 2025, members of VHP, ABVP, and Bajrang Dal staged a protest and raised Hindu religious slogans along the Bedipudia-Shivrampur Road at a school in Chitrakoot city (Uttar Pradesh), demanding action against the school management whom the protesters accused of disallowing a student from sitting for his exams for chanting 'Jai Shri Ram' (Hindu religious slogan).

On 16 January 2025, local people and family members of the deceased staged a dharna (sit-in protest) along the Hoshiarpur-Chandigarh Road in front of the police station in Garhshankar city (Hoshiarpur, Punjab), demanding action against the in-laws of a woman for their suspected involvement in her suicide.

Around 16 January 2025 (as reported), a large number of Naga Sadhus (devotees of the Hindu god Shiva) staged a demonstration, vandalized banners and posters, and set stalls on fire near Old GT Pontoon Bridge in Allahabad city (Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh) during the Maha Kumbh (a Hindu festival) mela. On 16 January 2025, security guards and attendants of a family clashed at SN Medical College in Agra city (Uttar Pradesh) after the security guards were suspected to have stopped the attendants from meeting a patient.

On 16 January 2025, workers, land donors and cooks working under the water department held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) to demand regularization and increase in wages.
On 16 January 2025, MSJK members held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against the authorities over 15 children dying in Budhal area of Rajouri and demanded an investigation into the incident.

On 1 November 2025, residents of Antriksh Golf View 2 housing complex staged an indefinite sit-in protest in Sector 78 in Noida city (Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) against the mismanagement of the complex and poor maintenance.

On 1 November 2025, thousands of people led by INC members held a protest at Rangat town (North and Middle Andaman district, A&NI) over the continued negligence in repairing and completing National Highway-4 (NH-4) in North and Middle Andaman.

On 1 November 2025, a section of booth level officers held a protest at Kolkata city (WB) over their security and also demanded 'on-duty' status for their day time teaching jobs, when they can work for SIR exercise alone.

On 1 November 2025, five people assaulted and pelted stones at a Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MNREGA) inspection team in Banjaria village (Pilibhit, Uttar Pradesh) when the team arrived in the area to carry out an inspection of development works and tore official registers and documents during the inspection.
